scope_summary: Prime coat application for bare drywall wall surfaces in new construction. Single prime coat (no finish coats). Assumes drywall is taped, mudded, and sanded by drywall contractor prior to painting scope. Covers all paintable wall field area excluding openings. Does NOT include ceiling prime, wall finish coats, wood/panel walls, trim priming, drywall repair beyond normal joint compound, texture application, or stain blocking. Separate from ceiling prime because walls have different application considerations (vertical vs overhead, different spray patterns, different edge relationships). Separate from wall finish because prime happens before trim install and uses different material systems.
relevant_findings: PVA (polyvinyl acetate) primer is the standard choice for new drywall walls — same material systems as ceiling prime
Wall priming is typically done at the same time as ceiling priming in NC sequence, but wall application is faster than ceiling due to no overhead fatigue

Spray+backroll is the standard production method for walls in NC — spray-only is NEVER valid for priming bare drywall because backroll is always required for sealing and consolidation into drywall pores
Single primer coat is standard — walls have the same drywall absorption characteristics as ceilings
New construction drywall fasteners are mudded and rust-resistant — no spot-priming needed (inherits RC-001)
PVA and acrylic primers are sealers, not stain blockers — zero stain blocking capability (inherits RC-002)
Wall work is physically less demanding than ceiling work — no overhead fatigue factor. Production rates are 15-25% faster than equivalent ceiling prime rates
Wall height modifiers apply per Estimation_Modifiers_Doctrine line 170: height modifier applies to wall tasks when ceiling height creates elevated work areas. 18ft ceiling = 18ft walls
Floor protection varies by application method: roll = floor_perimeter (edge_only); spray/spray_backroll = floor_full for overspray containment
Drywall dust on walls must be removed before priming — HEPA vacuum or tack cloth for proper adhesion
Wall-to-ceiling edge cut-in is the inverse of ceiling's edge cut-in at wall line — same physical edge, different perspective. Wall uses PS_EDGE_LF.TO_CEILING, ceiling uses PS_EDGE_LF.TO_WALL

In NC sequence, wall prime typically occurs before trim installation. This means trim adjacency edges (baseboard, casing) are not present during prime phase — edge work is primarily at the ceiling line

Substrate inspection and repair is a QT-driven prep phase: QT2 does minimal inspection, QT3 does standard inspection and targeted repair, QT4 does comprehensive inspection and repair. This prep phase is included in the prime spec so it is self-contained

Cross-spec coordination note: if inspection/repair is performed during wall prime, the finish spec (SF_DRYWALL_WALL_NC_FINISH) should eliminate its first inspection/repair round to avoid double-counting

condition_drivers.impact: Drives inspection/repair intensity. QT2: minimal inspection (major defects only). QT3: standard inspection with targeted repair. QT4: comprehensive inspection with thorough repair. Does NOT differentiate primer application itself — primer must be applied properly at all tiers.

Drives production rates, protection requirements, and edge work strategy. Spray+backroll is standard NC production. Roll for smaller jobs or occupied spaces. Spray-only is NEVER valid for priming bare drywall — backroll is always required for sealing.
Height modifier tiers per Estimation_Modifiers_Doctrine: standard (7-8ft) = 1.0, tall (9-12ft) = 1.3, high (13-17ft) = 1.5, extreme (18ft+) = 2.0. An 18ft ceiling means 18ft walls.
Affects coverage rate and absorption. Level 3 = more absorption (unsealed joints more visible under primer). Level 4 = standard NC. Level 5 = uniform surface, may require high-build primer.
Texture affects coverage rate (more paint per SF on textured surfaces) and nap selection. Smooth = baseline, orange_peel = 1.10x, knockdown = 1.15x.

quality_differences.description: Minimal quality. Minimal inspection — major defects only (unfilled joints, exposed fasteners). No targeted repair beyond obvious deficiencies. Primer application standard is unchanged — no drips, sags, or holidays.

Standard quality. Standard inspection with work light at raking angle to reveal defects. Targeted repair of identified defects (nail pops, unfilled joints, damaged paper). Primer application standard is unchanged.
quality_differences.inspection_level: Walk with work light, mark and repair defects
quality_differences.repair_scope: Targeted — fill identified holes, address nail pops, repair damaged paper face

quality_differences.description: Premium quality. Comprehensive inspection with systematic scan. Thorough repair of all identified defects. More time spent on inspection and repair. Primer application standard is unchanged — additional requirement may include verifying consistent mil thickness.
quality_differences.inspection_level: Systematic scan with raking light, comprehensive defect marking
quality_differences.repair_scope: Thorough — all defects addressed, feathered edges, uniform surface prep

failure_modes.consequence: Primer does not adhere properly, leading to peeling or flaking at touch/tape removal. Dust creates a separation layer between drywall and primer film.
failure_modes.mitigation: HEPA vacuum with brush attachment before priming — never skip

failure_modes.consequence: Bare drywall spots absorb finish coat unevenly, causing visible flashing (sheen variation). Especially visible on smooth walls under raking light.
failure_modes.mitigation: Backroll consolidation, proper spray technique with overlapping passes, visual inspection before leaving room

failure_modes.consequence: Insufficient sealing of drywall porosity. Finish coat absorbs unevenly, causing flashing and uneven sheen. Coverage rate and topcoat holdout are compromised.
failure_modes.mitigation: Follow product data sheet for coverage rate. Do not over-extend primer.

failure_modes.consequence: Spray dries before backroll can consolidate. Results in orange peel, texture variation, lap marks. Film build is uneven.
failure_modes.mitigation: Backroller sets the pace per Estimation_Modifiers_Doctrine. Spray rate must not exceed backroll rate.

failure_modes.consequence: Overspray settles on unprotected or poorly protected floors. Especially damaging on finished hardwood, tile, or LVP.
failure_modes.mitigation: Full floor protection (floor_full zone) for all spray methods. Rosin paper on hard floors, plastic on carpet.

prep_requirements.method: HEPA vacuum with brush attachment OR tack cloth for small areas
prep_requirements.reason: Drywall dust reduces adhesion and causes contamination in primer film. Walls accumulate more dust than ceilings due to vertical surface area and gravity settling patterns.

prep_requirements.method: Walk with work light at raking angle to reveal defects, mark with pencil/chalk
prep_requirements.reason: Identify fastener pops, unfilled joints, damaged paper, screw dimples not fully filled. Raking light is critical for wall inspection — direct overhead light hides defects.
prep_requirements.skip_conditions: QT2 reduces to major defects only

prep_requirements.method: Fill identified defects with lightweight spackle or joint compound, sand smooth when dry
prep_requirements.reason: Defects filled before prime create a uniform surface for finish coats. Primer seals repairs. Repair intensity is QT-driven.
prep_requirements.skip_conditions: QT2 minimal repair. Repairs beyond normal joint compound are drywall contractor responsibility.

limitations: Zero stain blocking — sealer only, not a stain blocker (RC-002)
Lower adhesion and build than acrylic latex

advantages: Better adhesion and build than PVA

wall_specific_considerations.impact: Wall work is performed at a natural standing position (for standard height). No overhead body fatigue. Production rates are 15-25% faster than equivalent ceiling tasks.
wall_specific_considerations.rate_adjustment: Wall rates are the baseline; ceiling rates are the reduced version

wall_specific_considerations.impact: Standard 7-8ft walls: work from floor with extension pole for upper areas. 9-12ft: step ladder for upper cut-in and rolling. 13-17ft: scaffold or baker staging. 18ft+: scaffold, possibly lifts. Height modifier applies per Estimation_Modifiers_Doctrine.
wall_specific_considerations.rate_adjustment: Height modifiers: H1=1.0, H2=1.3, H3=1.5, H4=2.0

wall_specific_considerations.impact: Wall spray is horizontal or vertical pattern at comfortable working height. Less physical strain than ceiling spray. Overspray falls downward to floor, not onto operator.
wall_specific_considerations.rate_adjustment: Wall spray rate is baseline; ceiling spray is ~15% slower

wall_specific_considerations.impact: Backrolling walls is done with roller on extension pole at natural height. Less fatiguing than ceiling backroll. Better roller control — fewer drips than overhead work.
wall_specific_considerations.rate_adjustment: Wall backroll rate is baseline; ceiling backroll is ~20% slower

wall_specific_considerations.impact: Wall spray creates overspray that falls to floor. Floor protection required for spray methods (floor_full zone). Roll method requires only perimeter drops (floor_perimeter zone). Protection requirements are less intensive than ceiling spray because overspray pattern is more directional.
wall_specific_considerations.rate_adjustment: Protection setup time varies by method

wall_specific_considerations.consideration: NC sequencing — trim not yet installed
wall_specific_considerations.impact: In typical NC sequence, wall prime occurs before trim installation (baseboard, casing). This means wall edges at trim locations are not relevant during prime phase. Primary edge work is at the ceiling line only. After trim install, wall finish spec handles trim adjacency edges.
wall_specific_considerations.rate_adjustment: Fewer edge work items than a repaint wall spec

required_paintscope_keys.description: Total paintable wall field area (excluding openings)
required_paintscope_keys.required_when: Always — primary quantity driver for wall priming

required_paintscope_keys.description: Linear footage of wall-to-ceiling boundary for edge cut-in from the wall's perspective. Distinct key from ceiling's PS_EDGE_LF.TO_WALL — each surface declares its own edge relationship.
required_paintscope_keys.required_when: When application_method is roll, or when spray requires edge work at ceiling line

paintscope_key_resolution.PS_SURFACE_SF.WALL_FIELD: EXISTS in catalog and mapping table (Section 2.1, IN_SF_WALL_FIELD)
paintscope_key_resolution.PS_EDGE_LF.TO_CEILING: EXISTS in catalog and mapping table (Section 2.2, IN_LF_EDGE_TO_CEILING)

zones.rationale: Roll method has minimal drip risk — perimeter drops along base of walls sufficient for catching drips and roller splatter.
zones.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to floor_full when application_method is spray or spray_backroll

zones.condition: when application_method is spray or spray_backroll
zones.rationale: Wall spray creates overspray that falls to floor. Full floor coverage required to prevent floor damage.
Any fixtures installed before priming (outlets, switches, light fixtures) need protection from overspray. In NC, fixtures may or may not be installed at prime time.

protection_zones_analysis.notes: Wall prime in NC does NOT typically require ceiling_line protection (ceiling is also being primed or is bare). Wall_adjacent protection is not needed (this IS the wall spec). Trim_edges protection is not needed because trim is not yet installed in NC sequence.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Wall and ceiling are almost always different products (different primer tints possible, definitely different finish coats). Edge work at ceiling line is the primary adjacency concern during wall prime. In NC, both may be primed in same session — but edge discipline still required to maintain clean boundary.

Baseboard is typically NOT installed during wall prime in NC sequence. This adjacency is declared for project-level finish group optimization but does not create edge work tasks in the prime spec. Becomes relevant in wall finish spec.

Door casing is typically NOT installed during wall prime in NC sequence. Declared for project-level adjacency tracking. Wall primer should cover through door opening areas; finish spec handles casing adjacency.

Window casing is typically NOT installed during wall prime in NC sequence. Declared for project-level adjacency tracking. Wall primer should cover through window frame areas; finish spec handles casing adjacency.

affected_conditions.notes: Floor protection material selection and inclusion: rosin paper on hard floors, plastic on carpet for spray methods. Subfloor does not require protection (RC-003). In NC, floors may or may not be installed at time of wall prime.

Wall height determines access equipment. Standard 7-8ft walls = none. 9-12ft = step_ladder. 13-17ft = scaffold. 18ft+ = scaffold/lift. Height modifier values from Modifier_Registry: H1=1.0, H2=1.3, H3=1.5, H4=2.0.
affected_conditions.modifier_notes: Height modifiers applied via production.json, not site_condition_rules directly

conditions_not_applicable.reason: New construction — building is vacant by definition. No furniture protection needed. If NC project has unusual occupancy, handle as project-level exception.
New construction — no existing paint, no lead possible. lead_status = not_applicable.
New construction drywall should be dry. If active moisture present, stop work — this is a building envelope issue, not a painting condition.
Relevant to product performance but not task inclusion/exclusion in spec. Product data sheet governs temperature limits. NC buildings typically have HVAC operational before paint phase.
Placeholder condition per Site_Condition_Vocabulary_Reference. No tasks currently reference it.
NC projects operate on builder schedules. Time pressure is a project-level concern, not spec-level. No task inclusion/exclusion driven by time_constraint for wall prime.

adjacency_notes.scope_impact: Primary edge work in wall prime. Cut-in at ceiling line required for roll method. Spray method may also require edge touch-up at ceiling line depending on spray technique and ceiling status.
adjacency_notes.nc_context: In NC, ceilings and walls are typically primed in same session. Wall primer should stop at ceiling line without extending onto ceiling surface. Same physical edge as ceiling's PS_EDGE_LF.TO_WALL but from wall's perspective.

adjacency_notes.scope_impact: Trim is typically NOT installed during NC wall prime. These adjacencies are declared for project-level optimization but do not create edge work tasks in this spec.
adjacency_notes.nc_context: Baseboard, door casing, and window casing are installed after prime phase. Wall primer extends through these future trim locations.

notes_for_materials_manager: Same material systems as ceiling prime — PVA for QT2-QT3, acrylic latex for QT4, high-build for Level 5
Coverage rates are the same as ceiling prime (same drywall substrate, same absorption) — typically 350-400 SF/gal for PVA, 300-350 SF/gal for acrylic, ~200 SF/gal for high-build
Spray tip selection: 517 standard for primer on drywall walls
Roller nap selection: 1/2" for smooth drywall, 3/4" for orange peel or knockdown texture
18-inch roller for spray+backroll production, 9-inch for roll-only
Floor protection materials vary by method: perimeter drops for roll, full rosin paper or plastic for spray
No stain blocking products — PVA/acrylic are sealers only (RC-002)
No dry times in specs (RC-004) — reference PDS
notes_for_sop_librarian: Mirror ceiling prime SOP structure with wall-specific task IDs (TSK_WALL_* prefix)
Vacuum/dust removal step is CRITICAL — same as ceiling spec (RC-001 applies: no spot-priming of fasteners)
Spray+backroll coupling constraint: backroller sets pace per Estimation_Modifiers_Doctrine
Edge cut-in is at CEILING line (not wall line) — inverse of ceiling spec. Uses PS_EDGE_LF.TO_CEILING
Floor protection: floor_perimeter for roll, floor_full for spray/spray_backroll
No trim masking needed — trim is not installed during NC wall prime
No ceiling_line masking needed — ceiling is either bare or being primed simultaneously
Include substrate inspection/repair as QT-driven prep phase: QT2 minimal, QT3 standard, QT4 comprehensive
Cross-spec coordination: flag that if inspection/repair done here, SF_DRYWALL_WALL_NC_FINISH should skip its first inspection/repair round
notes_for_estimation_engineer: Wall production rates are FASTER than ceiling equivalents — no overhead fatigue factor
Roll rates: ~350 SF/hr smooth wall (vs ~300 ceiling), ~275 SF/hr textured (vs ~235 ceiling)
Backroll rates: ~400 SF/hr wall (vs ~325 ceiling) — no overhead fatigue
Effective spray+backroll rate = backroll rate (coupling constraint per Estimation_Modifiers_Doctrine)
Cut-in rates: ~100 LF/hr wall ceiling-edge (vs ~85 ceiling wall-edge) — working at comfortable height
Height modifiers per Modifier_Registry: H1=1.0 (7-8ft), H2=1.3 (9-12ft), H3=1.5 (13-17ft), H4=2.0 (18ft+)
Inspection/repair rates are QT-driven: QT2 has minimal time (0.8x), QT3 baseline, QT4 comprehensive (1.3x)
Floor protection setup is less scope than ceiling spray protection (ceiling needs full room; wall spray also needs full room but overspray pattern is more directional)
assumptions: All drywall is standard gypsum board (not specialized types like moisture-resistant or fire-rated)
New construction surface condition is 'Good' — minimal defects expected from drywall contractor
Standard wall height 7-8 ft is baseline; height modifiers apply above that
Drywall contractor has completed all taping, mudding, and sanding before paint crew arrives
Walls and ceilings are typically primed in the same session in NC production
Trim (baseboard, casing) is NOT installed during wall prime phase (typical NC sequence)
Floor protection is conditional on floor_type per RC-003 — subfloor needs no protection
HVAC is operational providing adequate ventilation and temperature control
uncertainties: Exact wall vs ceiling production rate differential — 15-25% range needs field validation
Whether wall spray+backroll rate is closer to 400 or 450 SF/hr baseline
Floor condition at time of wall prime — site_condition_rules handle this via floor_type
Whether fixture_covers zone is commonly needed during NC wall prime (depends on electrical/plumbing schedule)

inherited_research_corrections.title: No spot-priming NC drywall fasteners
inherited_research_corrections.impact: No spot-prime tasks in wall spec — fasteners are covered by drywall contractor and modern screws are rust-resistant
inherited_research_corrections.source: SF_DRYWALL_WALL_NC_PRIME original research, codified in Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine

inherited_research_corrections.title: PVA/acrylic drywall primers have zero stain blocking
inherited_research_corrections.impact: No stain blocking claims in materials — PVA and acrylic primers are sealers only
inherited_research_corrections.source: SF_DRYWALL_WALL_NC_PRIME original research, codified in Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine

inherited_research_corrections.title: Floor protection conditional on floor_type
inherited_research_corrections.impact: Site condition rules for floor_type drive floor protection task inclusion: subfloor = no protection, finished/partial = protection required

inherited_research_corrections.title: Do not specify dry times in specs
inherited_research_corrections.impact: No dry time references in wall spec — too many variables, reference PDS instead

cross_spec_coordination.deduplication_note: If substrate inspection/repair is performed during SF_DRYWALL_WALL_NC_PRIME, the finish spec SF_DRYWALL_WALL_NC_FINISH should eliminate its first inspection/repair round to avoid double-counting labor. This is tracked via a cross_spec_flag in the SOP modules.
cross_spec_coordination.shared_session_note: Wall prime and ceiling prime (SF_DRYWALL_CEILING_NC_PRIME) are typically performed in the same work session. Project assembly should optimize shared protection setup/teardown across both specs.

research_corrections.title: Spray-only is never valid for priming bare drywall
research_corrections.description: Backroll is ALWAYS required when primer is sprayed on bare drywall. Drywall must be sealed — if not sealed, even sheen on finishes is impossible. Spray-only application_method has been removed from this spec.
research_corrections.source: Stakeholder directive (Eric) — declared as gospel doctrine
research_corrections.impact: application_method config dimension reduced to ['roll', 'spray_backroll']. No spray-only modules, tasks, rates, or crew configs.
